t: A tiny 20-pin chip for touch buttons, sensors, and long-lasting battery gadgets.
steps: Buy the Adafruit ATtiny1616 Breakout from Adafruit, Pimoroni, or The Pi Hut.
Get a USB serial adapter and a resistor to act as a UPDI programmer.
Get a breadboard and some jumper wires to connect the breakout.
Install the free Arduino IDE and add the megaTinyCore board package.
Wire the adapter to the UPDI pin and pick SerialUPDI as the programmer.
Pick ATtiny1616 from the board list and open the Blink example.
Click Upload and watch an LED on the breakout start to blink.
